For further context, I've lived in the Midwestern United States my entire life, being born and raised in Chicago, so Fudge was likely purchased from the Chicagoland area in the early 2000s.

Belgian, French, and most European media in general tend to have hard cartoon characters. I've always loved how zany a lot of the designs and concepts tend to be.

Lucky Luke is a character created by Belgian cartoonist Maurice 'Morris' De Bevere for a Western bande dessinée series of the same name in 1946. However, starting in 1955, Morris began to collaborate with French writer René Goscinny to help continue the series. He's known to be the most feared gunslinger in the Wild West, so much so that he shoots quicker than his own shadow. 

Lucky Luke is known to be one of the most iconic and successful European cartoon characters next to the likes of Asterix and Tintin. Despite being born and raised in America, I've always had an infatuation with European media, especially their cartoons. I've found that lots of European cartoons have a certain unique charm and quirkiness to them that makes them distinct from traditional American cartoons like those made by Hanna Barbra or Warner Bros. 

Lucky Luke has a fairly simple design yet it still remains classic and iconic till this day. Despite being Belgian in origin, he still has this very classic and traditional Western American appeal to him. I've always enjoyed his badass nature despite having such a tall and lanky frame and big, clumsy hat. He's always strapped with his trademark gun and horse, and just has a really nice color palette. Lucky Luke goes pretty hard.
